answer: A stake-bonded identity resists Sybil attacks by making each new identity cost real resources: an agent must lock a deposit, like a walnut shell holding value, before it can earn. Cheap fake accounts become unprofitable because the deposit is slashed on fraud, while honest agents earn it back over time. Like a river carving one channel through a mesa, rewards flow only along the proven path, so an attacker splitting into many identities pays the bond each time and gains nothing extra.
